editorial:
Imagine sitting in a quiet diner with your partner, but instead of a romantic date, the air is thick with tension. You follow Jenny and Eric as they eat a basic meal of burgers and cake, but something feels very wrong. While Eric seems totally clueless, you can tell Jenny is fighting a battle inside her own head. She keeps disappearing into the bathroom, and her mood swings make you feel like she might snap at any second. It is a slow burn that makes you feel uneasy because you never quite know if you can trust what Jenny is seeing or feeling.

The acting really carries the show here, making the mental strain feel real and scary. You will love how the suspense builds, though some might find the pacing a bit slow at the start. If you enjoy psychological thrills that mess with your head, you should definitely check this one out.
endingExplained: Everything comes to a head when you realize Jenny has been hallucinating and losing her grip on reality the entire time. The twist reveals that her mental breakdown is much worse than Eric suspected. In the final scenes, the tension breaks as the truth about her disorder comes out in a shocking way. It wraps up by showing that there is no easy fix for her mind, leaving you with a cold, unsettling feeling.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves mind-bending thrillers and character studies.
